age.evidence: Male Swiss mice (18-22 weeks old; 35-45 g)

sex.evidence: only male mice were employed in this study

dosing.evidence: Drugs were diluted in 0.9% NaCl and administered acutely via intraperitoneal injection (i.p.) 24 h before the test session of the learned helplessness model.
S-ketamine 10 or 30 mg/kg (ip)... administered acutely via intraperitoneal injection (i.p.)

handling.evidence: Methods do not mention a handling protocol prior to testing.

group_housing.evidence: Mice were housed in groups of up to eight per cage (41 × 34 × 16 cm), until the beginning of experiments. Single-housed cohort was isolated 7 days before learned helplessness for the second experimental step.

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12:12 h light--dark cycle, lights on at 6:00 a.m.

assays.assay_description: Home cage observation 10-15 min post-injection; rearing counts, lid-climbing time, grooming time, and time stopped manually scored from video.

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed in the home cage located in the animal facility

food_restriction.evidence: food and water available ad libitum (home cage)

water_restriction.evidence: food and water available ad libitum (home cage)

time_to_assay.evidence: video recorded in the interval between 10 and 15 min after treatments

sample_size.evidence: vehicle n=16, S-ket 10 n=9, S-ket 30 n=5, DMT 10 n=12, DMT 25 n=6 (Table 1)

outcomes.summary: DMT at both doses (10 and 25 mg/kg) significantly reduced exploratory behaviors (rearing, lid-climbing) and increased time stopped 10 min post-injection. S-ketamine 30 mg/kg (but not 10 mg/kg) also altered gross behavior.
outcomes.statistics: rearings F(4,43)=7.81; lid-climbing F(4,43)=3.66; grooming F(4,43)=4.39; stopped F(4,43)=4.20, p<0.05
outcomes.evidence: DMT at both doses tested, 10 and 25 mg/kg, significantly reduced exploratory behaviors (such as rearing counts and time of lid-climbing) and increased time stopped

B1_num_measures.evidence: rearing counts, time spent lid-climbing, grooming, time stopped

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Single 5-min observation window; no within-session bins reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: rearing, grooming (i.e., self-cleaning), lid-climbing are natural mouse behaviours

B7_automated_classification.evidence: manually quantify gross behaviors detected for each mouse by a blinded experimenter

E1_environment_type.evidence: mice were placed in the home cage located in the animal facility

E8_food_water.evidence: food and water available ad libitum (home cage)

D2_session_duration.evidence: video recorded in the interval between 10 and 15 min after treatments (5 min)

assays.assay_description: Shuttle box (50×30×30 cm) with two compartments separated by guillotine door; mice received inescapable footshocks across 2 induction days, then 30 escapable footshock trials at screening (day 3) and test (day 4, 24 h post-drug). Escape frequency and latency recorded.

application_type.evidence: administered acutely via intraperitoneal injection (i.p.) 24 h before the test session

setup_habituation.evidence: with the guillotine door closed, animals explored the shuttle box for 5 min (light off) before screening trials

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were individually placed in acrylic shuttle box and moved freely

food_restriction.evidence: No food in shuttle box during testing.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in shuttle box during testing.

time_to_assay.evidence: Twenty-four hours after drug administration (day 4), mice underwent a test session

sample_size.evidence: Group-housed: vehicle n=11, S-ket10 n=7, DMT10 n=9; single-housed: vehicle n=16, S-ket10 n=9, S-ket30 n=5, DMT10 n=12, DMT25 n=6

outcomes.summary: S-ketamine and DMT (both 10 mg/kg) reversed escape deficits in group-housed helpless mice 24 h post-injection (increased escapes, reduced latency), but neither drug at any tested dose reversed helplessness in single-housed mice.
outcomes.statistics: Group-housed escapes: F(2,20)=4.10, p=0.03; latency treatment F(2,80)=7.60, sessions F(3,80)=14.70, interaction F(6,80)=2.41, p<0.05. Single-housed: p>0.05
outcomes.evidence: In group-housed mice, S-ketamine and DMT (both at 10 mg/kg)... reversed helpless behavior... the treatment with S-ketamine and DMT, even at higher doses, did not abolish the helpless behavior in single-housed mice

B1_num_measures.evidence: escape latency and frequency of escapes were recorded

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Escape latencies in the screening and test sessions, analyzed in blocks of 15 escapable footshock trials

B4_ethological.evidence: Escape behaviour not in ethological repertoire category per rubric.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Learned helplessness involves a learned stimulus-shock association.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Animal mobility...was manually scored by an experimenter blinded to treatment conditions

E2_shelter.evidence: No enclosed refuge in shuttle box.

E6_spatial.evidence: divided into two compartments by a guillotine door

D1_continuity.evidence: screening session (day 3) and test session (day 4); both reported

D2_session_duration.evidence: 30 trials with ~20 s mean ITI plus 5-min exploration in screening ≈ 15-20 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: screening day 3 + test day 4 = 2 recording days

D4_baseline.evidence: Screening session prior to drug treatment provides baseline behavior for analysis.

D5_followup.evidence: Test session 24 h after drug administration.

assays.assay_description: Two-bottle choice (2% sucrose vs water) for 12 h in home cage; sucrose preference and total liquid intake measured at baseline (pre-stress), 48 h, and 5 days post-drug.

setup_habituation.evidence: animals were habituated to two bottles (A and B), both containing 2% sucrose solution, for ~12 h during the dark phase

water_restriction.evidence: mice were deprived of water for 4 h immediately before re-exposure to the bottles

time_to_assay.evidence: 48 h (or 3 days) and 5 days after drug-treatment

sample_size.evidence: vehicle n=9, S-ket10 n=7, S-ket30 n=4, DMT10 n=7, DMT25 n=6 (Table 1)

outcomes.summary: Both DMT doses (10 and 25 mg/kg) and S-ketamine prevented the stress-induced reduction in sucrose preference at 5 days post-treatment. S-ketamine 30 mg/kg increased total fluid intake.
outcomes.statistics: RM ANOVA F(2,16)=3.71, p=0.04; total intake S-ket30 F(2,6)=40.28, p<0.05
outcomes.evidence: both S-ketamine and DMT (at all doses tested) significantly prevented the reduction of sucrose preference observed in the control group 5 days after treatments

B1_num_measures.evidence: sucrose preference (%) and total liquid ingestion

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Between-session comparisons only; total over 12 h period.

B4_ethological.evidence: Preference score; not ethological per rubric.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Testing was performed in helpless individually housed mice... in the home cage

E8_food_water.evidence: 12 h of access to one bottle containing 2% sucrose and another containing water

D1_continuity.evidence: baseline, 48 h and 5 days after drug-treatment

D4_baseline.evidence: Baseline measurements were taken after the sucrose solution habituation period, and before footshock stress sessions

assays.assay_description: Mice suspended by tail >50 cm above floor for 6 min; immobility time manually scored during final 4 min at 28 h, 120 h, and 192 h post-drug.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were suspended by the tail using adhesive tape

time_to_assay.evidence: 28 h, 120 h, and 192 h after drug-treatment

sample_size.evidence: 28h: vehicle n=13, S-ket10 n=9, S-ket30 n=5, DMT10 n=12, DMT25 n=6 (Table 1)

outcomes.summary: S-ketamine 30 mg/kg reduced immobility at 28 h. DMT 10 mg/kg reduced immobility with effects persisting up to 8 days post-injection, longer-lasting than S-ketamine.
outcomes.statistics: Mixed effects analysis, treatment effect F(4,43)=3.56, p<0.05
outcomes.evidence: S-ketamine (only at 30 mg/kg) reduced the immobility time in helpless mice at 28 h... DMT 10 mg/kg trended to evoked a similar effect up to 8 days after drug injection

B4_ethological.evidence: TST immobility not ethological per rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: manually recorded during the final 4 min by an observer

D1_continuity.evidence: 28 h, 120 h, and 192 h after drug-treatment

D5_followup.evidence: 120 h and 192 h are >=24 h after drug administration

assays.assay_description: Square arena (40×40×40 cm) under low red lighting; 30 min recording with Anymaze tracking. Total distance, distance in 5-min blocks, % center time and % center distance (first 10 min) measured.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were individually placed in the center of a square arena

time_to_assay.evidence: open field test was performed ~30 h after treatment

sample_size.evidence: vehicle n=15, S-ket10 n=9, S-ket30 n=5, DMT10 n=12, DMT25 n=6 (Table 1)

outcomes.summary: DMT 10 mg/kg significantly increased spontaneous distance moved compared to vehicle at 30 h post-administration, reversing stress-induced hypolocomotion; effect prominent in first 15 min. No changes in center exploration.
outcomes.evidence: DMT 10 mg/kg, but not S-ketamine... 30 h after administration significantly increased the spontaneous distance moved compared to vehicle-treated mice

B1_num_measures.evidence: Total distance, distance in 5-min blocks, % center time, % center distance

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: distance moved analyzed in blocks of 5 min

B4_ethological.evidence: Locomotion/zone time not ethological per rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: analyzed with Anymaze® software (position tracking, not behavioral classifier)

E3_bedding.evidence: arena was cleaned with 5% ethanol between trials; no bedding

D2_session_duration.evidence: Spontaneous exploration was recorded for 30 min

D5_followup.evidence: 30 h is >=24 h after drug administration.

assays.assay_description: Re-exposure to shock context for 3 min without footshocks; percentage of time freezing manually scored at 5 days and 8 days post-drug.

setup_restrain.evidence: re-exposed to the same context for 3 min, with the guillotine door open and the light on, without footshocks

time_to_assay.evidence: Contextual fear-expression tests were conducted at two post-conditioning intervals: 4 and 7 days (5 and 8 days after drug)

sample_size.evidence: 120 h: vehicle n=12, S-ket10 n=9, S-ket30 n=5, DMT10 n=4, DMT25 n=5 (Table 1)

outcomes.summary: DMT 10 mg/kg showed a non-significant trend toward reduced freezing at 5 days post-injection; S-ketamine had no effect. No significant effects at 8 days.
outcomes.evidence: a reduced percentage of freezing time was observed in helpless mice injected with DMT 10 mg/kg but it did not reach the significance (p = 0.10)

B6_cognitive.evidence: Contextual fear conditioning requires learned association.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: manually by an experienced observer blinded to treatment conditions

E1_environment_type.evidence: Same shuttle box used for conditioning.

E6_spatial.evidence: Shuttle box divided into two compartments by guillotine door.

D1_continuity.evidence: Tests at 5 days and 8 days post-drug.

D2_session_duration.evidence: re-exposed to the same context for 3 min

D5_followup.evidence: 5 and 8 days are >=24 h after drug.

assays.assay_description: EPM with open and closed arms; 5 min free exploration; % time in open arms and entries into closed arms manually scored at 5 days post-drug.

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to freely explore the apparatus for 5 min

time_to_assay.evidence: EPM test was conducted once 30 min after contextual fear conditioning in helpless mice 5 days after drug-administration

sample_size.evidence: vehicle n=12, DMT10 n=5, DMT25 n=5 (Table 1, EPM block)

outcomes.summary: DMT 10 and 25 mg/kg increased time spent in open arms at 5 days post-administration, indicating anxiolytic-like effects; S-ketamine had no effect.
outcomes.evidence: DMT 10 and 25 mg/kg, but not S-ketamine 10 and 30 mg/kg, increased the time spent exploring the open arms

B1_num_measures.evidence: % time in open arms and entries into closed arms

B4_ethological.evidence: Zone preference; not ethological per rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: manually scored by a trained observer

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms not shelter per rubric.

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM arms not distinct compartments per rubric.

assays.assay_description: After 7 h food deprivation, mice placed in brightly lit open-field arena with food pellet at center for 5 min; latency to feed and consumption recorded in unfamiliar and familiar (home cage) environments at 8 days post-drug.

setup_restrain.evidence: individually placed in a brightly lit open-field arena... allowed to explore for 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: After 7 h of food deprivation, mice were individually placed in a brightly lit open-field arena

time_to_assay.evidence: NSFB test was conducted once in helpless mice 8 days after drug-administration

sample_size.evidence: vehicle n=12, S-ket10 n=9, S-ket30 n=5, DMT10 n=5, DMT25 n=6 (Table 1)

outcomes.summary: Neither DMT nor S-ketamine significantly affected latency to eat or food consumption in the NSFB test at 8 days post-administration.
outcomes.evidence: neither DMT nor S-ketamine significantly affected the behavior of mice in the novelty-suppressed feeding behavior 8 days post-drug administration

B1_num_measures.evidence: Latency to begin eating and time spent ingesting food, in both unfamiliar and familiar environments

B4_ethological.evidence: Latency/consumption metrics; not scored as ethological per rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: manually recorded by a blinded experimenter

E8_food_water.evidence: single food pellet positioned at the center

judge_notes: Both candidates agreed on the 8 assay structure: gross home-cage behavior, learned helplessness, sucrose preference, TST, OFT, contextual fear conditioning, EPM, NSFB.
Added S-ketamine as a second dosing entry (qwen omitted it); paper explicitly tested S-ketamine 10 and 30 mg/kg as comparator.
Group_housing scored 'yes' (qwen) rather than 'not_reported' (gptoss): paper explicitly states 'Mice were housed in groups of up to eight per cage'.
Sucrose preference D2 session duration: 12 h access = >6 h, scored 3 (consistent with gptoss).
Learned helplessness B6 cognitive scored 1 — the paradigm depends on a learned shock-context association.
EPM E6 scored 0 per rubric explicit instruction that EPM arms are not multiple compartments.
Time_to_assay value_minutes uses the first/earliest timepoint per rubric guidance for 'multiple'.
